newsitem.title: FINLAND: Banking stocks bolster thin Helsinki, UPM slips.
newsitem.headline: Banking stocks bolster thin Helsinki, UPM slips.

text.p: * Gains in the banking sector following OKO's healthy nine-month profits help quiet bourse end modestly higher but tone seen wary ahead of U.S. elections on Tuesday. UPM-Kymmene hits 5-mth low as more analysts downgrade forestries.
* Vol FIM 159 million, 22 pct in Nokia

A healthy recovery in OKOBANK's January-September profits boosted hopes for the sector which led the bourse to a slightly higher close on Monday but trade was thin ahead of U.S. elections on Tuesday, brokers said.
"Investors are likely to remain sidelined until we get the results of the elections," one broker said.
President Clinton was expected to be re-elected easily, but stock markets could be hit if Republicans lost control of both houses in Congress, brokers said.
Merita A ended fair trade 0.40 markka up at 13.70 as OKO's result sparked hopes for a strong Merita report on Thursday.
Analysts' median forecast for Merita's January-September earnings due for release on November 7 was a 952 million markka operating profit after credit losses.
OKOBANK's swung to a 248 million markka nine-month operating profit after credit losses from a 32 million loss.
The share closed moderate trade at a new 53.90 markka 28-month high, up 1.90 or almost four percent. This was its highest close since June 1994.

UPM closed at a five-month low 89.40 markka, down 1.10 -- its lowest close since May 30 -- as more analysts downgraded forest industry sector. Morgan Stanley was reported to have cut a number of American paper industry shares.
Ferry operator Silja failed to rise on improved nine-month earnings and closed thin trade flat at 32.00 markka.
Analog mobile phone maker Benefon retained its upward trend after announcing a cooperation deal with Swedish Ericsson last week and the share ended fair trade 3.00 markka higher at 83.00.
Nokia closed modest trade 1.50 markka up at 210.50.
